points.description: States that a nonlinear classifier can handle data that is not linearly separable (which a linear classifier cannot classify correctly).
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only says nonlinear is 'better' or 'more accurate' for some data without mentioning non-separability.

points.description: States that a nonlinear classifier can form more complex (curved/non-straight) decision boundaries.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if vaguely says it is more flexible or powerful without mentioning boundaries.

rubric.notes: Full marks if the student says nonlinear classifiers work on data that cannot be separated by a straight line/hyperplane and/or can make more complex boundaries, in any wording. Either idea stated clearly with a reasonable link to the other can earn 2. Vague claims like 'more accurate' earn part marks; wrong or unrelated answers earn 0.
